headline: Headline profit jumps on a weak comp, not real strength
summary_short: PepsiCo's Q2 FY2026 net revenue rose 6.4% year-over-year to $24.18 billion and diluted EPS more than doubled to $2.18, but the prior-year quarter included a $1.9 billion impairment charge that depresses the comparison base; core (non-GAAP) diluted EPS grew a more modest 4% to $2.20.
summary_long: Reported operating profit rose 125% and net income 136% year-over-year, but almost entirely reflects a weak comparison: Q2 2025 carried a $1.9B impairment on the Rockstar and Be & Cheery brands. Core (non-GAAP) diluted EPS, which excludes that and other items, grew a more modest 4% to $2.20. Organic revenue growth was 2% (1 point volume, 2 points net pricing); PBNA's 7% reported growth was driven mainly by the poppi acquisition against an organic volume decline, while PFNA fell 2% on unfavorable net pricing. Gross margin slipped 44bp y/y to 54.2% as cost of sales grew faster than revenue. Free cash flow (24-week YTD) was $1.17B, up from a $342M outflow. No new forward guidance was disclosed in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Reported profit growth is dominated by a $1.9B prior-year impairment on the Rockstar and Be & Cheery brands depressing the Q2 2025 base, per the filing's comparability reconciliation; core (ex-items) results grew far more modestly.
Organic revenue growth of 2% (1pt volume, 2pt net pricing), plus favorable FX, partially offset by the net impact of acquisitions and divestitures, per the segment organic-revenue table.
GAAP diluted EPS growth mirrors the net income swing versus a impairment-depressed Q2 2025 base; core (non-GAAP) diluted EPS grew a more modest 4% to $2.20.
Tracks the operating profit swing versus the Q2 2025 impairment-depressed base, plus a higher effective tax rate this quarter (22.0% vs 18.6%), per the income statement.
Consolidated pretax income tracks the same operating-profit swing versus the prior-year impairment-depressed base.

Margin expansion of 8.7ppt is primarily the absence of the prior-year $1.9B brand impairment, plus productivity savings and effective net pricing, partially offset by operating cost increases, per the MD&A.

Cost of sales grew faster than net revenue in the quarter (up from the same-quarter base), narrowing gross margin; the filing does not break out a specific commodity or mix cause at the consolidated level.
